key_insight: The paper shows that trapped non-wetting droplets in capillary tubes can be unpinned by non-resonant acoustic streaming, with the strongest efficiency occurring when the acoustic absorption coefficient matches half the inverse droplet distance.
engineering_relevance: This provides a design rule for lowering transducer power while improving droplet mobilization in porous media, with direct relevance to downhole acoustic recovery and capillary-flow control.
method: Derive a second-order hydrodynamic model for acoustic-wind force density in narrow capillaries.
Combine bulk acoustic streaming with background static pressure gradients to compute the critical amplitude needed to overcome capillary pinning.
Include wall-boundary and core thermo-viscous dissipation to identify the optimum condition α = 1/(2x₀).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivation and numerical validation, plus cross-correlation against legacy industrial frequency baselines, to support the proposed optimal operating condition.
watch_item: The model is theoretical and idealized, so performance may shift in real porous media where geometry, fluid properties, and attenuation vary spatially.
paper_title: Unpinning of trapped oil droplets via non-resonant acoustic streaming in capillary tubes
